findings.rationale: Update norms are near zero against the median client (median norm ratio ~0.01, z=-13.4). Per-round data show norm_ratio exactly 0 in 11 of 20 rounds (including rounds 15-20), and all other rounds are below ~0.3. This matches uploading the global model back without training. Local performance was not used to rule this out.

Median norm ratio is ~0.003 (z=-8.2), with exact-zero updates in 11 of 20 rounds (e.g. rounds 1, 3, 8-11, 13, 16-18, 20). The remaining rounds are also far below the median norm. This is the free-rider signature of returning the global model without local training.

Median norm ratio is ~0.002 (z=-5.4), and min norm ratio z=-8.1. Exact-zero updates appear in about half the rounds (5-9, 11, 12, 16, 17, 19). The other rounds are mostly tiny (0.02-0.18), with a single larger round (round 20, 0.40) that does not match a consistently trained client. This is consistent with intermittent free-riding.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup tools, then confirmed the strongest leads. Three clients (HI, KS, MI) have near-zero update norms, with exact-zero uploads in roughly half of rounds. That matches the free-rider fault, so I report them with onset round 1. I found no consistent evidence of label noise, prevalence shift, poisoning, drift, missing-value sentinels, subgroup bias or explanation instability. Other single outliers (e.g. AL drift, NV age-group outcome rate, MA income-group O/E, GA/WV age-group FNR, feature-tail z-scores in NM, DC, PR, NH) were small-client noise and did not persist across rounds or tools. Budget used: about 18.8 of 20 epsilon.
